title: A Rails provider adapter you can replace
outcome: Keep provider request formats outside the business use case and normalize failures.
cue: Keep the business contract yours; keep vendor details at the edge.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Keep provider request formats outside the business use case and normalize failures.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: A fake adapter test does not prove a live model behaves correctly. A “provider-compatible” endpoint can differ in schema support, tool IDs, errors, and response item types.

trace.title: Rails use case
trace.detail:
Define a small application-owned interface such as propose_filter or explain_facts. A provider adapter builds the vendor request, sets deadlines, maps response items, and returns your own result/error type. Controllers should not know whether a provider calls something input, messages, output, or toolResult.

Capabilities still differ. Do not hide missing schema, tool, streaming, or modality support behind a uniform method name. Validate the selected combination at configuration time. Keep model identifiers in environment/configuration and record the effective version used in evaluations.

The official OpenAI Ruby SDK used in this course requires modern Ruby. The isolated lab uses Ruby 3.3 and Rails 7.2. A Ruby 2.7 / Rails 4.2 application may use a supported HTTP boundary or a separate modern gateway. Do not install this lab's gems into an existing legacy application.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Controller → use case → adapter interface → provider response → normalized result → domain validator. Use a fake adapter for deterministic business tests. Use separate adapter contract tests for request/response mapping and separate labelled online evaluation for model behavior.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A fake adapter test does not prove a live model behaves correctly. A “provider-compatible” endpoint can differ in schema support, tool IDs, errors, and response item types.
